skip_reason: Unscored pending the Walkthrough Scheduler Mini-Rubric (still marked PENDING in the rubric, needs Amanda + Cameron decision) — customer was already flagged for a virtual walkthrough on home size and was handed off live, so pricing/clock/estimate/Save Your Ass were correctly never raised.
top_strength: She recovered a missed callback cleanly and escalated the speed of the handoff twice in ninety seconds. The customer opened cold and slightly unsure — 'just the first time that I'm talking to you I don't know how this works' — and she absorbed it without friction: 'Okay, no, no problem at all.' She pre-empted the biggest objection on a soft move date before he could raise it, volunteering 'we do have a flexibility with that, so there are no fees if you do have to change the date or modify or anything like that,' which matters because he had just told her the October 29th date was a placeholder. She confirmed the walkthrough path rather than assuming it, 'this was also for a a walkthrough as well. Right? A virtual walkthrough,' and when he said he was free immediately she did not park him on a callback — she booked a concrete twenty-minute window with a named person, 'I have Nicole who can do the virtual walkthrough with you... it's 1:40. Would you be available at two?', then upgraded that to a live transfer when a second option opened: 'actually, I might be able to get you on over to Eric actually.' Naming the colleague, naming the time, and beating her own quoted window is exactly the behavior that stops walkthrough leads leaking between the intake call and the estimate.
coaching_note: The one thing worth changing is that she let the customer define the job and never wrote it down. He gave her a material scope detail unprompted — 'it's not like a, like a to move the entire house because I'm moving to a very close by at the house and I have a lot of time to move. So I'm gonna do all the boxes and small things while you come and get the big stuff' — and her entire response was 'Okay. Perfect.' That is a partial-load, short-haul, big-items-only job, which is a completely different quote from the whole-house move the walkthrough was originally booked against, and Nicole or Eric now has to rediscover it from scratch. Thirty seconds of capture before the transfer — big items only, boxes handled by the customer, short local move, date still soft — makes the walkthrough faster and the estimate more accurate, which is the whole point of routing this call to a walkthrough in the first place. She should also pin the date rather than leave it floating; she correctly told him there is no fee to change it, but nothing was held, so a customer who is genuinely flexible now has no reason to commit. On tenure versus habit: this is a tenure gap, not a habit one. Her instincts are right — she confirmed the routing, removed the date objection, and beat her own callback window — and what is missing is the handoff-notes discipline that comes from having been burned by a re-interview, which at three months in she has not been yet.
phone_presence_notes: Warm and reassuring with a nervous first-time caller — 'Okay, no, no problem at all' and 'Okay, you got it' landed naturally, she explained the internal scramble transparently rather than leaving dead air ('We're like all talking to each other right now'), and the customer went from 'I don't know how this works' to 'Okay, awesome' and 'That's good' within a few minutes.
audio_review_reason: Thin evidence base — 6.1 minutes, 39 transcript lines, and the recording cuts off mid-transfer ('Alright, give me just one moment') so the actual handoff, the close and any final rapport are simply not captured. The warmth markers present are real but sparse, and the customer's side is mostly one-and two-word acknowledgments, which the transcript cannot distinguish between comfortable brevity and disengagement. Ears would settle whether this is a 4 or a 3.
